title: Mary, mother of the Church (CCC 963–970)
hookLine: her role points always to her son

lines: HER HAND POINTS TO THE CHILD.
cards: There's a kind of icon, very old, that you'll find in Greek, Russian and Catholic churches alike. Mary holds the child Jesus on one arm. Her face isn't turned to you, exactly.
Her other hand is open, palm up, gesturing toward the child. The icon's Greek name is Hodegetria: she who shows the way. People sometimes imagine Catholic devotion to Mary as a spotlight on her.
In this picture, she's pointing away from herself.

teach.h: WHATSOEVER HE SHALL SAY, DO YE.
teach.b: Start at a wedding in Cana. The wine runs out. Mary tells Jesus, then turns to the servants and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye."
It's the last thing John's Gospel records her saying. Not look at me. Do what he tells you.
Then the cross. Jesus sees his mother and the disciple he loved standing by. "Woman, behold thy son."

Then to the disciple: "Behold thy mother." From that hour, John says, the disciple took her into his own home. Catholics read that disciple as standing for every believer: Jesus giving his mother to the whole Church.
During the Second Vatican Council, Pope Paul VI gave her the title Mother of the Church. The Catechism says her place in the Church can't be separated from her union with Christ.

It calls her the Church's model of faith and love, who prays for the Church as a mother prays for her children. And it's careful: her role in no way hides or takes away from Christ as the one mediator.

teach.h: IT SHOWS CHRIST'S POWER, NOT HERS.

teach.b: Orthodox Christians honor her deeply as Theotokos, God-bearer, and ask her prayers too. Many Protestants honor her as the mother of Jesus and a model of faith, but don't pray to her.

Catholics pray the Hail Mary, which begins with the angel's greeting in Luke: "Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women." And at its middle, the prayer names her son: Jesus.

how: Catholics pray the Hail Mary on its own and in the rosary, and since 2018 keep the memorial of Mary, Mother of the Church, on the Monday after Pentecost.

o: the mother of Jesus, who points people to her son
the first woman, made in the garden of Eden
a goddess Catholics worship alongside God

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
p: whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye

s: the Catechism says Mary's role takes something away from Christ
it says her role in no way obscures Christ as the one mediator; it shows his power.
Mary's last recorded words in John's Gospel point to Jesus
whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye.
all Christians pray to Mary in the same way
Catholics and Orthodox ask her prayers; many Protestants honor her but don't pray to her.

games.q: you're Mary at the wedding in Cana. the wine has run out. you've told Jesus. what do you say to the servants?
o: whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye.
tell the guests to go home.
games.why: she sends them to him. it's the last thing John records her saying, and it sums up her role.

practice: If you pray it, pray one Hail Mary slowly for the whole Church, its people, its wounds, its saints and sinners, giving each phrase a breath. If you don't, picture the old icon instead: the mother, the child, the open hand.
Follow where the hand points, and rest your attention there.

wordCard.voice: Mary. The mother of Jesus, whom Catholics call Mother of the Church: a model of faith, whose whole role, the Church says, is to point to her son. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek form of the Hebrew name Miriam, the name of Moses's sister.

carryVoice: Your line: she points to him. Tomorrow, the last things begin. That's day three hundred twenty-three.
